title: The Blackout Banquet
subtitle: A dark reception. A smoking alibi. Follow the circuit, not the caterer.

consultation.speaker: Benny
consultation.text: The charity reception went dark during the awards. Victor says my hot plate sabotaged the lights.

consultation.speaker: Oliver
consultation.text: Was it connected to a wall socket?

consultation.speaker: Benny
consultation.text: It runs on a battery. The only thing I plugged was my lunch special.

consultation.speaker: Oliver
consultation.text: Then we need the equipment photograph and the electrical records. An accusation needs a circuit.

opening.speaker: Bumble
opening.text: We will establish why the lights failed. Nobody is to demonstrate it by touching the wiring.

opening.speaker: Victor
opening.text: The vendor arrived. The room went dark. My entrance was ruined. Three connected tragedies.

opening.speaker: Oliver
opening.text: Connected is exactly the question. Let us identify what was actually drawing power.

opening.speaker: Bumble
opening.text: Milo, give us your observations. Keep your conclusions on a separate plate.

evidence.title: Battery hot plate
evidence.description: 20:24. The equipment check shows a hot plate on a blue battery cassette. No mains lead is attached.
evidence.inspection: The signed equipment check identifies a 48 V self-contained battery. The wall socket behind the table is empty. Benny was not drawing power from the stage circuit.

evidence.title: Breaker event log
evidence.description: The stage circuit was healthy at 20:20. Its protective breaker tripped at 20:32:04.
evidence.inspection: A time-stamped protective trip occurred twelve minutes after Benny arrived. This was an overload trip, not a manual switch-off.

evidence.title: Reception circuit plan
evidence.description: Stage circuit capacity: 2,300 W. The serving urn uses 1,500 W on that circuit.
evidence.inspection: The urn leaves 800 W of spare capacity. The vendor table is labelled BATTERY EQUIPMENT; the stage extension also feeds the presentation riser.

evidence.title: Signed effects cue sheet
evidence.description: Victor rented a 1,200 W fog machine. Cue V: start it at 20:32 for the award presentation.
evidence.inspection: Victor signed the rental and the 20:32 activation cue. The machine was connected to the presentation riser, on the same circuit as the urn.

evidence.title: Electrician load test
evidence.description: The electrician reproduced the trip using the urn and fog machine. Benny's battery unit was isolated.
evidence.inspection: 1,500 W plus 1,200 W equals 2,700 W: 400 W above the circuit limit. The protective breaker tripped again. The cause was the event setup, not the battery hot plate.

evidence.title: Breaker inspection tag
evidence.description: No damaged wiring or tampering was found. The breaker opened automatically and reset after the fog machine was unplugged.
evidence.inspection: This supports an automatic safety response. There is no evidence of a deliberate interruption or a connection from Benny's equipment.

statements.text: Benny set up his hot plate at the vendor table.
statements.press: MILO: I checked the equipment at twenty-four minutes past eight.

statements.text: His hot plate was plugged into the stage power.
statements.press: MILO: I assumed every hot thing needed a wall socket. OLIVER: What does your signed check actually show?

statements.text: There was an extension lead behind the serving urn.
statements.press: MILO: It ran towards the presentation riser, behind the urn.

resolution.speaker: Oliver
resolution.text: Your signed photograph shows a battery cassette and an empty socket. The hot plate was electrically isolated.

resolution.speaker: Milo
resolution.text: I inspected it correctly and remembered it creatively.

resolution.speaker: Brick
resolution.text: I have obtained the effects cue sheet. Victor signed for a fog machine.

resolution.speaker: Victor
resolution.text: Atmosphere is a perfectly legitimate expense.

statements.text: The failure happened at 20:20, the moment the vendor arrived.
statements.press: VICTOR: I remember a dark cloud. OLIVER: An emotional recollection is not a breaker timestamp.

statements.text: The fog machine was scheduled for the award presentation.
statements.press: VICTOR: At twenty thirty-two. A majestic entrance requires precision.

statements.text: The serving urn was already operating before the speeches.
statements.press: BRICK: One thousand five hundred watts. The circuit plan records it.

resolution.speaker: Oliver
resolution.text: The breaker remained healthy at 20:20. It tripped at 20:32:04, immediately after your scheduled effects cue.

resolution.speaker: Bumble
resolution.text: Enter the electrician's test and inspection. We require a cause, not merely a suspicious minute.

resolution.speaker: Brick
resolution.text: The test reproduced the failure. Nobody touched a manual switch.

resolution.speaker: Victor
resolution.text: I would prefer the word dramatic to the word overloaded.

statements.text: A fog machine is harmless theatrical equipment.
statements.press: VICTOR: It uses twelve hundred watts. I assumed charisma supplied the rest.

statements.text: The urn alone stayed below the circuit limit.
statements.press: OLIVER: Correct. Now account for the second device on the same circuit.

statements.text: The vendor must have caused the trip; the event equipment could not.
statements.press: VICTOR: The electrician tested both event devices together. I object to arithmetic.

resolution.speaker: Oliver
resolution.text: The urn and fog machine drew 2,700 watts on a 2,300-watt circuit. The electrician reproduced that exact overload.

resolution.speaker: Bumble
resolution.text: And the inspection found no tampering. This was a safety breaker doing its job.

resolution.speaker: Victor
resolution.text: My entrance briefly exceeded the building's capacity for me.

closing_prompt: Account for the disconnected hot plate, the 20:32 trip, and the reproduced overload. What caused the blackout?
conclusions: The urn and fog machine overloaded the stage circuit. Benny's battery unit was isolated.
Benny secretly switched off the lights when he arrived at 20:20.
The serving urn alone exceeded the 2,300-watt limit.

verdict.speaker: Bumble
verdict.text: The equipment photograph excludes the battery hot plate. The breaker log and load test identify an accidental overload.

verdict.speaker: Bumble
verdict.text: On the charge of sabotaging the reception: NOT GUILTY!

verdict.speaker: Benny
verdict.text: My hot dogs survived. Their dramatic lighting did not.

verdict.speaker: Victor
verdict.text: Next time I will request a dedicated circuit for my entrance.

verdict.speaker: Oliver
verdict.text: A complete explanation needs a connection, a time, and a cause. We finally have all three.
